blocks.h2: How Water Gets Into Algonquin Basements
blocks.intro: Most basement water here comes in one of four ways:

tiles.h3: The Sump Pump Couldn't Keep Up
tiles.body: When the Fox River is high, groundwater pours into the pit. A small or failing pump falls behind, and the pit overflows onto the floor.
No electricity, no pump. Without a battery backup, the pit fills during the very storm that caused the outage.

tiles.h3: Sewer Water Came Up the Drain
tiles.body: A blocked line or a full public sewer pushes water up through the floor drain or basement shower.

tiles.h3: A Tank or Hose Let Go
tiles.body: An original water heater or washer hose can flood a finished basement in minutes.

blocks.h2: The Fox River and Algonquin Basements
blocks.intro: The Fox River reached a record crest of 12.70 feet at Algonquin on April 23, 2013. In July 2017 it rose again, and homes on La Fox River Drive were threatened.

items.body: On April 23, 2013, the Fox River crested at a record 12.70 feet at Algonquin. Groundwater across a wide area rises with the river, and sump pumps run for days.
In July 2017, about 500 volunteers filled more than 25,000 sandbags as the river rose again, and Cornish Park was closed. Some residents still got water in their basements.

items.h3: Sump Systems Sized for Dry Years
items.body: Many builder sump pumps were sized for typical rain, not river years. Upgrading the pump and adding a backup is often the biggest single improvement.
A [sump pump with a battery backup](/algonquin/sump-pumps) for groundwater, a backflow valve for sewer water and, for repeat backups, an [overhead sewer system](/algonquin/overhead-sewer-systems).

bodies: Waterproofing keeps groundwater out of the basement. Our side of it is the plumbing that moves the water: sump pits and pumps, battery backups, discharge lines and the drain tile that feeds the pit.

If water comes in where the wall meets the floor, the drain tile may be clogged or the pump may not keep up when the river is high. We check the system and tell you what will actually stop the water. For water coming up through drains, see [sewage backup service](/algonquin/sewage-line-backup-services).

blocks.h2: Basement Flooding Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: What should I do the moment I find water in the basement?
items.preview: Stay safe, find the source and call.
items.answer: Keep clear of water near outlets and appliances. Check the sump pit: if the pump isn't running, check the breaker and the backup. If a pipe or appliance is leaking, close the main. Then call us.

items.q: Will a bigger sump pump help when the river is high?
items.preview: Often, yes, along with a backup.
items.answer: Often. If your pit fills faster than the pump can empty it, a higher-capacity pump helps. A battery backup or a second pump covers you if the first one fails.

items.q: Do homes far from the river flood too?
items.preview: Yes. Heavy rain affects homes well beyond the bank.
items.answer: Yes. Heavy rain raises groundwater and loads the sewers, so basements away from the river can still take on water.

items.q: Does homeowners insurance cover a flooded basement?
items.preview: It depends on the cause and your policy.
items.answer: It depends on the cause and the coverage. Sump pump failures and sewer backups usually need specific riders. Check with your agent before you need it.

items.q: What does basement flood repair cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the source and the fix. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on how the water got in and what it takes to stop it. We quote a flat rate for each option before we start.
